 West Central School District supports students and staff after tragedy 
 The loss of an elementary school student continues to affect the communities of Hartford and Humboldt, and resources are available so students can grieve. By Fiona Sullivan Published : Oct. 27, 2026 at 6:22 PM CDT Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google HARTFORD, S.D. (Dakota News Now) - The West Central School District is providing resources for students and staff after an elementary school student died over the weekend.
 The loss continues to affect the communities of Hartford and Humboldt. Teachers are making sure resources are available so students can grieve and process the loss.
 The district put its crisis plan into action to provide support heading into the week. The plan includes counselors and student success coordinators available in each building.
 “It went exactly how I thought it would go, that it would be extremely difficult, that students today, again, based upon that awareness, are able to express how they’re feeling in a very mature and real manner,” said Erick Knight, West Central superintendent. “They did that. It’s heartbreaking to see, but they did that.”
 Resources are also available for teachers and staff.
 “First day, we always think is the hardest, and so we had more support there,” said Knight. “We also, this morning, through some benefits that we have, we have three counseling sessions that are available to every employee and kind of sent that out and just encourage them if they were at a place that they needed some of that help that they would reach out and get that support.”
 Other tragedies occurred over the past few days, with Flandreau and Corsica reeling from two major car accidents. Knight said it’s more emotions to process.
 “The same thing this morning, unfortunately, having to reach out to another superintendent saying that we’re here, we’re here to support,” said Knight. “However, we can help if there’s language or if there’s scripts or if there’s counseling supports that are needed. We’re a small, close-knit state in terms of school administration as well, and so we’re here to help and support.”
 The district is continuing to provide support and counseling services this week and going forward as students continue to attend classes.
